commands.name: Pass
commands.doc: Sends the message of the event being handled on, unchanged. Only inside OnNoteOn, OnNoteOff, OnCC, OnPitchBend, OnProgramChange and OnOther.

fields.name: delayMs
fields.doc: send this many milliseconds after the event whose hook calls it

fields.name: delayTicks
fields.doc: send this many clock ticks after the event (added to delayMs)

commands.name: Panic
commands.doc: Ends every sounding note now, drops everything that was waiting and sends All Notes Off on all channels.

commands.name: SetTimer
commands.doc: Starts (or restarts) a timer; its hook OnTimer(id) is called when it is due. The delay is the length of ms and ticks together and is fixed when the timer is set. It counts from the event whose hook sets it.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: delay in clock ticks, added to ms (the length of a tick at the present tempo)

fields.name: repeating
fields.doc: fire again and again after the same delay

hooks.name: OnStart
hooks.doc: Runs once after the script is loaded.

hooks.name: OnNoteOn
hooks.doc: A note on arrived. Channels count from 1.

hooks.name: OnNoteOff
hooks.doc: A note off arrived (or a note on with velocity 0, then velocity is 0).

hooks.name: OnPitchBend
hooks.doc: A pitch bend arrived; value is -8192 to 8191.

hooks.name: OnOther
hooks.doc: Any other message of 1 to 3 bytes except the real-time messages (channel pressure, poly pressure, song position ...): the status byte and the two data bytes (0 when absent).

hooks.name: OnTick
hooks.doc: A tick of the tempo clock (while the transport runs); tick counts from 0 at the start.

hooks.name: OnTransportStart
hooks.doc: The transport started; the clock begins with tick 0.

hooks.name: OnTimer
hooks.doc: A timer set with SetTimer is due.

enums.name: Ticks
enums.doc: Lengths of notes in ticks of the clock (24 per quarter note).

libraries.summary: chord shapes as lists of semitones above the root.

members.name: notes
members.doc: the MIDI notes of the chord, those above 127 left out

members.name: invert
members.doc: the chord with the lowest note moved up an octave, `times` times

libraries.summary: helpers for steps on the clock (24 ticks per quarter note).

members.name: swing
members.doc: ticks to delay step number `step` (counting from 0): the odd steps are pushed back by amount (0 to 0.5) of a step

members.name: euclid
members.doc: a list of `steps` booleans with `pulses` of them true, spread evenly

libraries.summary: scale shapes as lists of semitones above the root, and the nearest note of a scale.

members.name: quantise

examples.title: Pass everything through
examples.summary: Every message goes on unchanged. Shows that a message only goes on when its hook calls Pass(): a message without a hook (for example MIDI clock) is dropped. Start from this one when a script should change only some messages, and remove the Pass() of the kind you want to handle yourself.
examples.code:
-- Pass everything through
-- Every message goes on unchanged. Shows that a message only goes on when its hook calls Pass(): a message without a
-- hook (for example MIDI clock) is dropped. Start from this one when a script should change only some messages, and
-- remove the Pass() of the kind you want to handle yourself.
function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity) Pass() end
function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity) Pass() end
function OnCC(channel, controller, value) Pass() end
function OnPitchBend(channel, value) Pass() end
function OnProgramChange(channel, program) Pass() end
function OnOther(status, data1, data2) Pass() end

examples.title: Transpose
examples.summary: Every note is moved up by a number of semitones (negative moves it down). The note off has to go to the same note as its note on, even if the setting changed in between, so the script remembers what it sent. Change the shift.
examples.code:
-- Transpose
-- Every note is moved up by a number of semitones (negative moves it down). The note off has to go to the same note as
-- its note on, even if the setting changed in between, so the script remembers what it sent. Change the shift.
local shift = 7

local sent = {} -- [channel][note] = the note that went out for this key

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity)
    local out = clamp(note + shift, 0, 127)
    sent[channel] = sent[channel] or {}
    sent[channel][note] = out
    NoteOn(channel, out, velocity)
end

function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity)
    local out = sent[channel] and sent[channel][note]
    if out then
        sent[channel][note] = nil
        NoteOff(channel, out)
    end
end

function OnCC(channel, controller, value) Pass() end
function OnPitchBend(channel, value) Pass() end

examples.title: A chord from one note
examples.summary: Every key sounds a minor seventh chord on top of it, strummed 15 ms apart. Shows the library "chords" and the delayMs field. The note off is strummed the same way, so a short key press cannot end a note before it began. Change the shape (Chords.Major, Chords.Sus4 ...) or the strum.
examples.code:
-- A chord from one note
-- Every key sounds a minor seventh chord on top of it, strummed 15 ms apart. Shows the library "chords" and the delayMs
-- field. The note off is strummed the same way, so a short key press cannot end a note before it began. Change the
-- shape (Chords.Major, Chords.Sus4 ...) or the strum.
import "chords"

local shape = Chords.Minor7
local strumMs = 15

local sounding = {} -- [channel][note] = the notes that this key switched on

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity)
    local notes = Chords.notes(note, shape)
    sounding[channel] = sounding[channel] or {}
    sounding[channel][note] = notes
    for i, chordNote in ipairs(notes) do
        NoteOn(channel, chordNote, velocity, { delayMs = (i - 1) * strumMs })
    end
end

function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity)
    local notes = sounding[channel] and sounding[channel][note]
    if notes then
        sounding[channel][note] = nil
        for i, chordNote in ipairs(notes) do
            NoteOff(channel, chordNote, { delayMs = (i - 1) * strumMs })
        end
    end
end

examples.title: Remap a controller
examples.summary: The mod wheel (CC 1) is sent as CC 74 (brightness), halved; all other controllers go through. Shows CC and Pass in one hook. Change the numbers, or the factor, to move any controller to another one.
examples.code:
-- Remap a controller
-- The mod wheel (CC 1) is sent as CC 74 (brightness), halved; all other controllers go through. Shows CC and Pass in
-- one hook. Change the numbers, or the factor, to move any controller to another one.
local from, to, factor = 1, 74, 0.5

function OnCC(channel, controller, value)
    if controller == from then
        CC(channel, to, math.floor(value * factor + 0.5))
    else
        Pass()
    end
end

examples.title: Quantise to a scale
examples.summary: Every note is moved to the nearest note of D dorian (a tie goes down). Shows the library "scales". The note off goes to the note that the note on went to. Change the root (0 = C ... 11 = B) and the shape (Scales.Blues ...).
examples.code:
-- Quantise to a scale
-- Every note is moved to the nearest note of D dorian (a tie goes down). Shows the library "scales". The note off goes
-- to the note that the note on went to. Change the root (0 = C ... 11 = B) and the shape (Scales.Blues ...).
import "scales"

local root = 2
local shape = Scales.Dorian

local played = {} -- [channel][note] = the note that went out

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity)
    local out = Scales.quantise(note, root, shape)
    played[channel] = played[channel] or {}
    played[channel][note] = out
    NoteOn(channel, out, velocity)
end

function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity)
    local out = played[channel] and played[channel][note]
    if out then
        played[channel][note] = nil
        NoteOff(channel, out)
    end
end

examples.title: A timed arpeggio
examples.summary: The held keys are played one after the other on a repeating timer, in an euclidean rhythm of 5 hits in 8 steps. Shows SetTimer (repeating, in ticks), OnTimer, StopTimer and the library "rhythm". The timer runs while a key is held. It plays on channel 1 at velocity 100; take both from the hook arguments to follow the player.
examples.code:
-- A timed arpeggio
-- The held keys are played one after the other on a repeating timer, in an euclidean rhythm of 5 hits in 8 steps. Shows
-- SetTimer (repeating, in ticks), OnTimer, StopTimer and the library "rhythm". The timer runs while a key is held.
-- It plays on channel 1 at velocity 100; take both from the hook arguments to follow the player.
import "rhythm"

local pattern = Rhythm.euclid(5, 8)
local held = {} -- the held notes, as they were pressed
local position = 0

local function remove(note)
    for i, heldNote in ipairs(held) do
        if heldNote == note then
            table.remove(held, i)
        end
    end
end

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity)
    if #held == 0 then
        position = 0
        SetTimer(0, { ticks = Ticks.Eighth, repeating = true })
    end
    remove(note)
    held[#held + 1] = note
end

function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity)
    remove(note)
    if #held == 0 then
        StopTimer(0)
    end
end

function OnTimer(id)
    if #held > 0 and pattern[position % #pattern + 1] then
        Note(1, held[position % #held + 1], 100, { lengthTicks = Ticks.Sixteenth })
    end
    position = position + 1
end

examples.title: All notes off when the transport stops
examples.summary: Notes go through, and when the host's transport stops every sounding note is ended. Shows OnTransportStop and Panic. Panic also drops everything that was waiting, so it is the right answer to a hung note.
examples.code:
-- All notes off when the transport stops
-- Notes go through, and when the host's transport stops every sounding note is ended. Shows OnTransportStop and Panic.
-- Panic also drops everything that was waiting, so it is the right answer to a hung note.
function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity) Pass() end
function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity) Pass() end

function OnTransportStop()
    Panic()
end

scripts.title: Arpeggiator: the keys you hold are played one after the other in time with the clock
scripts.summary: Change the settings below and save the file; copy it to user-1.lua on the device to make it your own.
scripts.code:
-- Arpeggiator: the keys you hold are played one after the other in time with the clock.
-- Change the settings below and save the file; copy it to user-1.lua on the device to make it your own.

local mode = "up"            -- "up", "down", "updown" or "random"
local rate = Ticks.Sixteenth -- ticks per step (Ticks.Eighth, Ticks.Sixteenth, Ticks.EighthTriplet ...)
local gate = 0.5             -- how long a note sounds, as a fraction of a step
local swing = 0.0            -- 0 to 0.5: the odd steps are late by this fraction of a step
local octaves = 1            -- how many octaves the pattern climbs

import "rhythm"

local held = {}              -- the held notes, as they were pressed
local channel = 1            -- played on the channel of the last key
local velocity = 100
local position = 0           -- where the pattern is, counted in steps since the first key

local function remove(note)
    for i, heldNote in ipairs(held) do
        if heldNote == note then
            table.remove(held, i)
            return
        end
    end
end

local function pattern()
    local sorted = {}
    for _, note in ipairs(held) do
        sorted[#sorted + 1] = note
    end
    table.sort(sorted)
    local notes = {}
    for octave = 0, octaves - 1 do
        for _, note in ipairs(sorted) do
            if note + 12 * octave <= 127 then
                notes[#notes + 1] = note + 12 * octave
            end
        end
    end
    return notes
end

function OnNoteOn(ch, note, vel)
    if #held == 0 then
        position = 0
    end
    remove(note)
    held[#held + 1] = note
    channel = ch
    velocity = vel
end

function OnNoteOff(ch, note, vel)
    remove(note)
end

function OnTick(tick)
    if tick % rate ~= 0 or #held == 0 then
        return
    end
    local notes = pattern()
    local count = #notes
    local index
    if mode == "down" then
        index = count - (position % count)
    elseif mode == "updown" and count > 1 then
        local cycle = 2 * count - 2
        local at = position % cycle
        index = at < count and at + 1 or cycle - at + 1
    elseif mode == "random" then
        index = math.random(count)
    else
        index = position % count + 1
    end
    local step = tick // rate
    Note(channel, notes[index], velocity, {
        delayTicks = Rhythm.swing(step, swing, rate),
        lengthTicks = rate * gate,
    })
    position = position + 1
end

scripts.title: CC Remap: controllers are turned into other controllers, everything else goes through
scripts.summary: Change the tables below and save the file.
scripts.code:
-- CC Remap: controllers are turned into other controllers, everything else goes through.
-- Change the tables below and save the file.

local remap = {
    [1] = 74,    -- mod wheel becomes CC 74 (brightness)
    [11] = 7,    -- expression becomes volume
}
local scale = {
    [11] = 1.0,  -- optional factor for the value of a controller (by its number before the remap)
}

function OnCC(channel, controller, value)
    local target = remap[controller]
    if target == nil then
        Pass()
        return
    end
    local out = math.floor(value * (scale[controller] or 1.0) + 0.5)
    CC(channel, target, clamp(out, 0, 127))
end

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity) Pass() end
function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity) Pass() end
function OnPitchBend(channel, value) Pass() end
function OnProgramChange(channel, program) Pass() end
function OnOther(status, data1, data2) Pass() end

scripts.title: Chord Player: every key you play sounds a chord on top of it
scripts.summary: Change the settings below and save the file.
scripts.code:
-- Chord Player: every key you play sounds a chord on top of it.
-- Change the settings below and save the file.

import "chords"

local shape = Chords.Major  -- Chords.Major, Chords.Minor, Chords.Dominant7 ... or your own list of semitones
local strumMs = 0           -- delay between the notes of the chord (0: all at once)
local inversion = 0         -- how often the lowest note is moved up an octave

local sounding = {}         -- [channel][note] = the notes that this key switched on

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity)
    local notes = Chords.invert(Chords.notes(note, shape), inversion)
    sounding[channel] = sounding[channel] or {}
    sounding[channel][note] = notes
    for i, chordNote in ipairs(notes) do
        NoteOn(channel, chordNote, velocity, {delayMs = (i - 1) * strumMs})
    end
end

function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity)
    local notes = sounding[channel] and sounding[channel][note]
    if notes == nil then
        return
    end
    sounding[channel][note] = nil
    for i, chordNote in ipairs(notes) do
        NoteOff(channel, chordNote, {delayMs = (i - 1) * strumMs})
    end
end

function OnCC(channel, controller, value) Pass() end
function OnPitchBend(channel, value) Pass() end
function OnProgramChange(channel, program) Pass() end

scripts.title: Octave Doubler: every note is played together with the same note some octaves higher or lower
scripts.summary: Change the settings below and save the file.
scripts.code:
-- Octave Doubler: every note is played together with the same note some octaves higher or lower.
-- Change the settings below and save the file.

local octaveShift = 1       -- 1: an octave up, -1: an octave down, 2: two up ...
local level = 0.7           -- velocity of the added note as a fraction of the played one

local added = {}            -- [channel][note] = the note that was added, or nil

function OnNoteOn(channel, note, velocity)
    Pass()
    local other = note + 12 * octaveShift
    added[channel] = added[channel] or {}
    added[channel][note] = nil
    if other >= 0 and other <= 127 and other ~= note then
        added[channel][note] = other
        NoteOn(channel, other, math.max(1, math.floor(velocity * level + 0.5)))
    end
end

function OnNoteOff(channel, note, velocity)
    Pass()
    local other = added[channel] and added[channel][note]
    if other ~= nil then
        added[channel][note] = nil
        NoteOff(channel, other)
    end
end

function OnCC(channel, controller, value) Pass() end
function OnPitchBend(channel, value) Pass() end
function OnProgramChange(channel, program) Pass() end

guide:
# Writing a MIDI Script script (guide for an AI assistant)

MIDI Script is a MIDI in, MIDI out plugin. Every incoming message is handed to a Lua script, and what the script sends
is what comes out: it can pass, change, add or drop messages and play things on the clock. This file tells you how to
work here. It holds no names, ranges or limits of the API: those are in `API.md` and `constants.lua` next to it,
generated from the plugin, and always right. Read them first.

## 1. What a script is, and what is in this folder

- A script is one Lua 5.4 text file. Its top-level code runs once when it is loaded. After that the plugin calls the
  hooks the script defines (global functions such as `OnNoteOn`), and the script answers by calling commands (global
  functions such as `NoteOn`, `CC`, `Pass`). A hook that is not defined is not called.
- **A message only goes out when the script sends it.** A message whose hook is missing, or whose hook sends nothing, is
  dropped. `Pass()` sends the message of the hook that is running, unchanged. The real-time messages (MIDI clock) have
  no hook and are not passed on.
- Files here: `API.md` (every command, hook, constant, library and limit), `constants.lua` (the named constants, already
  global in every script), `examples/` (small scripts that run as they are), the factory scripts (`passthrough.lua`,
  `arpeggiator.lua`, ...) and the libraries `chords.lua`, `rhythm.lua` and `scales.lua`. The factory scripts are read only.

## 2. Where a script goes

- On the Dwarf a script is a file `/data/jaypacks/scripts/midiscript/user-1.lua` up to `user-8.lua`. Reach it with
  `ssh root@192.168.51.1` and `scp -O`; the data partition survives a plugin update.
- Select it with the plugin's Script setting (User 1 to User 8). The factory scripts cannot be edited: to change one, or
  an example, copy it to a user slot.
- A script may `import "chords"`, `import "rhythm"` or `import "scales"` (factory libraries, see `API.md`); it cannot read
  other files, and `io`, `os`, `require` and `load` do not exist.

## 3. The loop to follow

1. Write the script to a user slot.
2. The plugin checks the file twice a second and reloads it after a save. Nothing is restarted.
3. Read `/data/jaypacks/scripts/midiscript/user-1.log` (same name as the script, `.log`). It says whether the load
   worked, the message with the line of an error, the calls that were ignored, and every line the script wrote with
   `Log(...)`. The plugin's Script status output shows the same in a number (1 ok, 3 compile error, 4 runtime error,
   5 over the budget, 6 out of memory). Late and Dropped count messages that missed their time or were lost.
4. Fix what the log says and save again.

A script that fails to load (syntax error, error at the top level or in `OnStart`) is rejected and the previous script
keeps playing, so a typo never silences the plugin; but the new script is not running either. Always read the log after
a save. An error in a hook ends the notes that call started, drops what it had queued, and the next event runs again.

## 4. Rules in short

- Hooks are global functions with fixed names and argument lists (`API.md`, Hooks). Write `function OnNoteOn(channel,
  note, velocity)`, not a local.
- Channels count from 1 in the hooks and in the commands. Notes and velocities are 0 to 127; a note on with velocity 0
  reaches `OnNoteOff`. Pitch bend is -8192 to 8191.
- Commands take positional arguments and, last, an optional table of named fields: `Note(1, 60, 100, { lengthTicks =
  Ticks.Sixteenth })`. Time is in milliseconds (`delayMs`, `lengthMs`, `ms`) or ticks (`delayTicks`, `lengthTicks`,
  `ticks`); the clock has 24 ticks per quarter note and `Ticks.Quarter` and the other lengths are in `constants.lua`.
- `Note` sends a note on and, one length later, its note off, which is certain even if the script is replaced. With
  `NoteOn` the script must send the `NoteOff` itself: remember what a key started, and send the note off to the same
  note (a transposing script that changed its setting in between would otherwise leave a note hanging). `Panic()` ends
  everything.
- `Pass()` works only inside the hooks for incoming MIDI (`OnNoteOn`, `OnNoteOff`, `OnCC`, `OnPitchBend`,
  `OnProgramChange`, `OnOther`), not in a timer or a tick.
- `OnTick` and the ticks of a timer need the clock: the host's transport (or the tempo the plugin reads); `OnTimer` is
  set with `SetTimer(id, { ms = ..., ticks = ..., repeating = true })`.
- `import "name"` runs a library once, then its global table is there (`import "scales"` gives `Scales`).
- Randomness is `math.random`; it gives the same numbers on every run. Keep state in locals at the top of the script.
- A hook has a small budget of instructions and milliseconds: no long loops.
- A number field outside its range is clamped. An integer argument (a channel, a note, a velocity, a timer id) outside its
  range, or not whole, makes the call ignored and is written to the log. A field name the command does not know is
  ignored and logged. A wrong type or a missing argument is an error in the hook.

## 5. Mistakes seen most

Each line is a message the plugin writes to the log, and the fix.

| Log says | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `NoteOn: 'channel' = 0 is outside 1..16, call ignored` | Channels count from 1 here. |
| `NoteOn: 'note' = 128 is outside 0..127, call ignored` | A transposed note must be clamped: `clamp(note + shift, 0, 127)`. |
| `NoteOn: 'velocity' = 0 is outside 1..127, call ignored` | A note on needs a velocity of at least 1. |
| `Note: 'velocity' = 63.5 is not a whole number, call ignored` | Round it: `math.floor(x + 0.5)`. |
| `Note: unknown field 'length' is ignored` | The fields are `lengthMs` and `lengthTicks`. |
| `Pass: Pass() works only inside a hook for incoming MIDI, call ignored` | Pass was called from a timer or a tick. |
| `CC expects 3 argument(s) and got 2` | A command called without all its arguments. |
| `CC: the last argument must be a table of fields, not number` | A value too many: named fields go in braces. |
| attempt to call a nil value (global 'noteOn') | A misspelt command or hook name. Names are case sensitive. |
| the script sounds like the previous one | It was rejected at load; the log has the reason. |
| notes hang | A `NoteOn` without its `NoteOff` (or the off went to another note). Use `Note`, or remember the note sent. |
| nothing comes out | The hook is missing or does not send: add `Pass()` or a command. |

## 6. The examples

| File | Shows | Uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `examples/01-pass-through.lua` | everything through; a message without Pass is dropped | OnNoteOn, OnNoteOff, OnCC, OnPitchBend, OnProgramChange, OnOther, Pass |
| `examples/02-transpose.lua` | a shift in semitones, remembering what each key sent | OnNoteOn, OnNoteOff, OnCC, OnPitchBend, NoteOn, NoteOff, Pass |
| `examples/03-chord-from-one-note.lua` | a strummed chord on every key | OnNoteOn, OnNoteOff, NoteOn, NoteOff, import "chords" |
| `examples/04-remap-a-controller.lua` | one controller turned into another | OnCC, CC, Pass |
| `examples/05-quantise-to-a-scale.lua` | every note moved into a scale | OnNoteOn, OnNoteOff, NoteOn, NoteOff, import "scales" |
